title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Mira Patel
content:
Overview:

This document is the canonical sales enablement playbook for Redwood Inference covering: positioning and messaging for target buyer personas, competitive brief summaries and battlecards, an audience-tailored pitch deck outline, pricing guidance and common objection-handling, two representative case studies with metrics, and a prospect-facing Security & Compliance FAQ.

Use cases: product teams integrating LLMs for customer-facing features, platform teams standardizing inference across business units, and enterprise security/compliance stakeholders evaluating private deployments.

Audience:
- SDRs and AEs engaging technical buyers
- Solutions engineers and pre-sales who need technical talk tracks
- Customer engineering and platform buyers evaluating deployment/ops needs

1) Positioning and Messaging

Core one-liner:
Redwood Inference: production-first LLM inference that delivers predictable latency, lower unit cost, and flexible deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) so engineering teams ship reliable, scalable, and secure AI features.

Top three value props (talk tracks by persona):
- Engineering/ML Engineer:
  - "Consistent, low-latency inference across hosted and private deployments — no surprises when you scale."
  - Talking points: SDK parity across modes, model version pinning, prefix/KV caching, quantization recommendations.
- Platform/Infra:
  - "Predictable unit economics and routing policies to control spend while meeting SLOs."
  - Talking points: batching profiles, autoscale policies, dedicated GPU pools, cost dashboards.
- Security/Compliance/CISO:
  - "Private control plane and optional on-prem package with KMS/HSM integration and audit logs."
  - Talking points: SOC 2/ISO readiness, VPC-only control plane, customer-managed keys, data residency controls.

Positioning pillars (short bullets you can use verbatim):
- Production-first: built-for-production SLOs, tracing, and rollout controls.
- Unified runtime: same API & SDK regardless of hosting model.
- Cost-aware controls: batching, caching, quantization recommendations with measured ROI.
- Enterprise-ready security: private deployments, KMS, audit logging, compliance artifacts.

2) Competitive Briefs (executive summary + battlecard)

Competitors covered: OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Cohere, Self-hosted runtimes (e.g., Triton/LLM infra vendors).

OpenAI (managed API):
- Strengths: best-in-class model capabilities, wide ecosystem adoption, simple developer experience.
- Weaknesses vs Redwood: limited deployment flexibility (no private on-prem control plane), less transparent performance/cost profiles, and fewer built-in rollout/observability controls for enterprise-scale inference.
- Win criteria: prospects who need private data residency, predictable unit economics, or on-prem air-gapped deployments.
- Talk track: "If you like the simplicity of hosted APIs but need predictable latency, cost control, or private deployment, Redwood gives you the same developer ergonomics with enterprise controls."

AWS Bedrock / Cloud vendors:
- Strengths: deep cloud integration, single-vendor stack, enterprise procurement alignment.
- Weaknesses vs Redwood: vendor lock-in risk, higher variability across regions, and less opinionated inference runtime optimizations for LLM-specific throughput/latency.
- Win criteria: customers looking to avoid lock-in, prioritize per-token cost control, or need advanced rollback/fallback policies across regions.

Self-hosted runtimes (Triton + custom infra):
- Strengths: full control, potential lower cost at extreme scale.
- Weaknesses vs Redwood: high engineering burden, lack of standardized SDK/console, and slower feature velocity for rollout/observability.
- Talk track: "We integrate with your KMS and VPC while removing the operational burden of building and maintaining your own inference stack."

3) Pitch Deck Outline (tailorable by buyer)

Slide flow (recommended 10-15 slides):
1. Title / 30s elevator
2. The problem (latency, cost unpredictability, ops complexity)
3. Redwood thesis: serving is the new competitive moat
4. Product overview (hosted API, Dedicated, Private)
5. How it works (serving runtime, batching, smart routing)
6. Security & compliance highlights
7. Performance benchmarks (latency P50/P95, throughput examples)
8. Pricing model & ROI example (see Pricing Guidance)
9. Case study 1 (SaaS customer)
10. Case study 2 (Enterprise private deployment)
11. Differentiation vs competitors
12. Implementation plan & timeline
13. Next steps / pilot proposal

Pre-sales tips:
- Lead with predictable latency and cost for technical buyers.
- Bring a solutions engineer for demos that include live latency dashboards and rollout examples.
- Use the dedicated offer to overcome procurement objections about SLAs and isolation.

4) Pricing Guidance & Objection Handling

Overview of published offerings (summary):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token pricing for generation/embeddings, suitable for rapid prototyping and low-to-medium volume production workloads.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly committed GPU pools, price per GPU-hour with predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): enterprise license + deployment fees, optional support tiers and compliance add-ons.

Common pricing playbook (simple heuristics):
- If ARR or monthly inference tokens exceed threshold X (e.g., $10k/mo spend), recommend Dedicated.
- If data residency or compliance required, recommend Private and include professional services in the proposal.
- For pilots: offer time-limited credits, a scoped POC with success metrics (latency, cost per 1M tokens), and a low-commit Dedicated trial if appropriate.

ROI example (high level):
- Baseline: Customer runs 1B tokens/month on competitor managed API at $0.0001/token = $100k/month.
- Redwood Dedicated plan reduces unit cost by 40% after reserved capacity and batching = $60k/month.
- Additional operational savings: 0.5 FTE platform engineering time saved (~$10k/month equivalent).
- Net savings: ~$50k/month.

Objection handling cheatsheet:
- "We already use a big cloud vendor": emphasize multi-cloud flexibility, lower lock-in risk, and better inference-specific runtime optimizations.
- "How do we control cost spikes?": explain autoscale caps, burst policies, quota limits, and per-route cost dashboards.
- "We need model quality guarantees": talk about model version pinning, canary rollouts, and evaluation/regression alerts tied to prompt sets.

5) Case Studies (two brief vignettes with metrics)

Case study: Conversational SaaS (Search augmentation feature)
- Customer profile: mid-market SaaS (product analytics), 500k MAU, product team integrating answer-generation into search.
- Challenge: unpredictable latency and per-token cost causing poor UX and cost overruns.
- Redwood solution: migrated to Redwood Hosted API for rapid onboarding, then to Dedicated for production. Enabled KV prefix caching and optimized batch sizes.
- Results (60-day): median latency reduced from 420ms to 120ms; monthly inference cost reduced 35%; error rate (timeouts/failed responses) reduced 88%.

Case study: Regulated Enterprise (financial services, private deployment)
- Customer profile: large enterprise with strict data residency and audit requirements.
- Challenge: must keep models and inference inside company network, integrate with corporate KMS, and demonstrate SOC2 controls.
- Redwood solution: Private deployment (VPC + HSM integration), dedicated support, rollout of short-lived inference keys and audit logging to SIEM.
- Results (90-day): compliance sign-off achieved, 99.95% uptime on Dedicated inference clusters, integration completed with existing alerting and change-control processes.

6) Security & Compliance FAQ (for prospects)

Q: Where does customer data reside when using Redwood Hosted API?
A: Customer data is processed in region-specific cloud regions; customers can select region at provisioning time. For regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployments to meet residency requirements.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) / HSM integration?
A: Yes. Private deployments and Dedicated plans offer integration with KMS providers and optional HSM/KMS for key storage. We support AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and customer HSM options for on-prem packages.

Q: Is communication encrypted in transit and at rest?
A: Yes. All network traffic uses TLS1.2+ with strong ciphers. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. For Private deployments, encryption keys may be customer-managed.

Q: What compliance certifications and evidence can you provide?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II evidence; we provide ISO readiness documentation and a compliance pack for enterprise customers. For HIPAA use cases we engage the legal and security teams to evaluate and provide a custom BAA where appropriate.

Q: How do you handle audit logging and retention?
A: We provide configurable audit logs for control-plane and inference events. Retention policies are customizable for Dedicated and Private customers; audit logs can be forwarded to customer SIEMs.

Q: What isolation guarantees are available?
A: Dedicated offers tenant isolation at GPU pool level with network separation. Private (VPC/on-prem) provides full isolation under customer control.

Q: How do you prevent model drift or data leakage between customers?
A: Our runtime enforces strict model and KV cache namespaces per tenant. We have automated tests in the model onboarding process to detect prompt leakage patterns and we recommend a private deployment for customers with the highest sensitivity.

7) Implementation & Pilot Plan (recommended 6-8 week pilot)

Pilot phases and milestones:
1. Week 0: Kickoff & scoping (owners, success metrics: latency P95, cost per 1M tokens)
2. Week 1-2: Integration & baseline measurement (SDK integration, sample prompts, auth setup)
3. Week 3-4: Optimization (batching, caching, quantization profiling if applicable)
4. Week 5-6: Canary/Demo to stakeholders (observability dashboards, cost dashboards, security review)
5. Week 7-8: Wrap-up & contract review (recommend Dedicated sizing or Private deployment plan)

Deliverables:
- Integration guide and runbook for SREs
- Performance & cost dashboard exports for the last 30 days
- Security/compliance pack for procurement

8) Sales Assets & Call-to-action

Key assets to attach to outreach:
- 10-slide deck template (see pitch deck outline)
- Two-pager ROI calculator (spreadsheet)
- Security & compliance pack (SOC2 artifacts, KMS docs, architecture diagrams)
- Demo script and pre-built demo environment (latency dashboard + canary rollout)

CTA options by stage:
- Early discovery: "Schedule a 30-minute tech discovery" with SE present.
- Mid-stage: "Run a 6-week pilot — our recommended scope is 1-2 endpoints and a performance baseline."
- Late-stage: "Procurement packet and Dedicated sizing worksheet"

Appendix A: Sample configuration table

| Component | Recommended default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Batch size target | 8-32 tokens/req | Tune for latency vs throughput trade-off |
| KV cache TTL | 24 hours | Increase for stable prompts (e.g., chat system prompts) |
| Canary percent | 5% | Start small for safe rollouts |
| SLA target (Dedicated) | 99.9% | Include rollback policy |
